title: Remaining-module audit repairs
status: All 23 audited defects and three additional observations repaired in source; not deployed
scope: Shared and edition-specific modules in School, Faith and Organisation editions, including their web and desktop entry points. Prior finance, academic, plan-management and tutorial-link changes were preserved.

repairs.change: New staff creation rejects existing usernames; web and desktop edits must name the original immutable account identity. Concurrent creation is create-only.
Staff saves and CSV imports check storage-ID and login-name collisions and preserve existing document IDs, including legacy IDs.

Staff imports validate their final administrator state. A shared atomic directory guard prevents concurrent management changes from removing the last active Super Admin. HR exits and staff restore use the same guard; self-service profile/password writes require the current record version.
Branch settings propagate failed reads instead of treating them as missing. Saves and resets preserve omitted fields and require the current version.

Restore stops when protected live settings cannot be read or their version is unknown; live identity and redacted credentials are preserved. Staff restore protects the signed-in administrator by actual destination ID and login aliases.
Enrolment uses the application's verified branch and section, reconciles existing legacy/scoped student records, and atomically commits student and application status with version conditions.
Clinic reads and writes require verified actor/module access and student scope; desktop records retain authoritative branch, section and student identity.
HR review updates authorize the stored review owner, reject reassignment and require the reviewed version.
Student Conduct requires the effective module entitlement and role capability on web and desktop, including read-only subscription enforcement.
Authorized manual attendance corrections replace the selected timestamp, recalculate daily metrics, reject impossible endpoint ordering and preserve historical/live clock state correctly.
School Store checkout records the exact stock document ID; payment processing resolves stock in its recorded branch and section. Ambiguous legacy codes are rejected.
Organisation Store direct-transfer approval resolves the stored stock document identity correctly.
Hotel operations enforce the actor's branch. The desktop bridge also applies effective hotel entitlement and subscription read-only access.
Hotel bookings and moves use shared room-version guards so simultaneous reservations cannot claim overlapping availability.
Reservation editor saves cannot bypass check-in/check-out transitions. Reservation, payment and charge updates share version guards so balance checks cannot use a stale reservation.
Clinic and kitchen stock movements commit inventory changes and movement logs atomically with current-version checks. Inventory metadata edits also reject stale writes.
Legacy desktop stock operations preserve immutable stock IDs and school scope, reuse guarded shared handlers, and reject negative stock.
Department responses omit confidential pastoral notes for actors without pastoral access.
Compact member edits preserve profile fields that were not submitted.
Service/program edits do not trust browser-submitted paid assertions and reject stale overwrites of offering state.
Organisation personnel, departments, meetings and programs accept appropriate edition-specific roles without granting pastoral or remittance privileges.
Organisation announcements use the proper recipient/composer rules, scheduler inclusion and push audience family.
Changing attendance breakdown mode clears obsolete totals rather than retaining stale breakdown values.
Batch department assignment preserves existing assignments instead of silently replacing them.
Visitor attendance requires a stable identity rather than accepting anonymous colliding entries.
Desktop bulk email has an in-progress guard and correctly restores controls after completion or failure.

validation.note: Synthetic local tests including loopback CBT server. Existing HTTPError cleanup ResourceWarnings and a Tk after-callback warning remain; unittest result was OK.

validation.command: git diff --check and JavaScript syntax checks

deploymentNotes: No source push, application compilation, release, deployment or production data mutation was performed in this repair session.

Deploy updated portal API and client assets together. Older staff editors that omit the explicit original identity are safely rejected when attempting an edit; refreshed web assets and a later desktop release provide that field.
The staff directory guard is created on the first authorized management change. Existing staff document IDs and passwords are not migrated by these repairs.
Hotel branch queries reject results exceeding the 1,000-record safety bound instead of silently computing partial availability or balances.

Existing overwritten accounts, malformed clinic records, duplicate enrolments, stock discrepancies and historical attendance totals are not rewritten automatically. Correcting existing records requires a separately reviewed reconciliation.

Runtime and concurrency tests use synthetic data and fault injection. Real payment processing, email/push delivery and physical-device workflows were not executed against production. Passing these tests is not a guarantee that every module is free of defects.
